text:
violet: Heads uptrying to run `redwoodctl init demo --local` on my Linux devbox (NFS-mounted $HOME) and it bombs during auth + never brings up localserve. anyone seen NFS weirdness?

ram: what do the logs look like?

violet: tiny paste: 
```
> redwoodctl init demo --local
device code flow started, visit https://redwood.auth and enter code Z9Y8-X7W6
waiting for auth...
login complete
warning: failed to persist profile: rename /home/violet/.config/redwood/profiles.json -> /home/violet/.config/redwood/profiles.json.tmp: invalid cross-device link
failed to start localserve: pid file exists at /home/violet/.local/redwood/localserve/pid (PID 8421)
```

ram: classic NFS cross-device rename. The CLI writes temp file in system tmp then renames; that fails if tmp and target are on different mounts. The pid file is likely from a previous run in a container.

violet: yep the PID 8421 is dead (zombie left from a container). `kill -0 8421` returns no process. Removing the pid file allowed localserve to start, but the profile still didn't persist so subsequent commands got 401.

ram: two quick workarounds: 1) set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR to a path on the same FS as your home before login: `export REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.config/redwood && mkdir -p $REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR` then `redwoodctl login --headless --profile=dev` 2) use headless token-file for CI and devcontainers: `redwoodctl login --headless --token-file=/path/on/samefs/rw.token`

violet: I tried REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR but the default tmpdir still got used by the CLI. I ended up creating a small wrapper: `TMPDIR=$HOME/.redwood-tmp redwoodctl login ...` which made the write succeed. Not ideal but unblocks.

ram: filed an issue for the CLI: it should perform atomic writes in the target dir (create temp file in same directory and then rename) or fallback to copy+unlink if rename fails. Also detect stale pid files and report the offending PID existence clearly instead of just "pid file exists".

ops-bot: Created ticket DX-5422: "redwoodctl: handle cross-device rename on NFS and improve localserve stale-pid diagnostics" (linked to devex/cli backlog) :eyes:

violet: also a small note about automation: our devcontainer reuses workspace and left old profiles.json with a broken merge state. I added `rm -f ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json` as a cleanup step in the image build to avoid merge errors during headless login.

ram: long-term we should add a `redwoodctl login --overwrite` flag for CI and a `redwoodctl localserve cleanup` helper to remove stale PID/pid.lock after verifying the PID is dead. For now, docs PR with the TMPDIR/REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR tips would help.

violet: thanks all, saving this thread so I don't forget the TMPDIR trick. :coffee:
